issues.description: New command names break the existing singular-dash convention (quickmark-save, bookmark-add).
issues.detail: Sibling commands use singular nouns (quickmark-add, quickmark-save, bookmark-add, bookmark-load), but this patch registers quickmarks-reload and bookmarks-reload (plural). The feature tests follow the plural form, compounding the inconsistency. Rename to quickmark-reload / bookmark-reload to match the surrounding namespace, or justify the break in the commit message.

issues.description: reload() is not atomic: a mid-parse failure leaves marks empty rather than preserving prior state.
issues.detail: reload() calls self.marks.clear() and then re-parses in place. If _init_lineparser or _parse_line raises, the manager is left with an empty marks dict while the on-disk file still holds the prior data, and changed has not fired with a coherent state. Build the new OrderedDict locally, then swap on success and emit.

issues.description: New BDD scenarios are unnamed, breaking the feature file's voice.
issues.detail: Every other scenario in urlmarks.feature has a descriptive title ('Saving a quickmark', etc.). The two added scenarios are bare 'Scenario:' lines, which hurts readability and test reports. Add titles like 'Reloading bookmarks from disk' and 'Reloading quickmarks from disk'.

issues.description: Feature scenarios assert the info message rather than actual reload behavior.
issues.detail: The new scenarios only check that an info string was printed, not that the on-disk change is reflected in the manager's state. The interesting test is: mutate the file, run the command, verify the new mark is present and the old one gone. Test the behavior the command exists for.

issues.description: Parse loop should be extracted as a pure helper so reload() is read, parse, swap, emit.
issues.detail: The refactor to delegate __init__ to reload() is the right direction but stops halfway. The loop body (skip blanks/comments, _parse_line) is the actual unit of work and belongs in a helper that takes lines and returns a dict. Then reload becomes value-construction followed by an identity swap, cleanly separating values from effects.

issues.description: reload() silently discards unsaved in-memory state with no docstring warning.
issues.detail: If a quickmark or bookmark was added but the save-manager has not flushed, reload() clears it without notice. For a user-invoked command this may be acceptable, but the docstring should explicitly state that unsaved changes are discarded so future maintainers do not have to reverse-engineer the contract.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the patch is small, well-scoped, and the refactor extracting reload() so __init__ delegates to it is good taste worth landing. Two issues block clean merge: command names break the existing singular-dash convention (quickmark-save vs the new quickmarks-reload), and reload() mutates self.marks in place so a mid-parse failure leaves the manager empty rather than preserving prior state — build a new value and swap atomically. Remaining nits are housekeeping: unnamed BDD scenarios, tests that assert the info message instead of actual reload behavior, the parse loop should be a pure helper, and the docstring should note that unsaved in-memory changes are discarded. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK on naming and atomicity before merge.
